one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 contains Q3 2026 results (forecast 2026-10-27 per AJ Bell [11]; guide core sales $4.9-5.0B, core EPS $0.85-0.89 [1]). Base rate from the last four prints in the daily series [4]: next-day moves of +15.6% (Jan-2026), -8.9% (Apr-2026), -12.1% (Jul-2026, a beat with in-line guide), -3.3% (Oct-2025) - average absolute move ~10%, and two of the last three were sell-offs on beats, so the reaction is about the Q4 guide versus a $20B exit run-rate target, not the quarter. Also in the window: hyperscaler Q3 capex commentary (late Oct) and possible ATM share issuance [9] as an overhang. No directional edge: centred on $156.68 with a lognormal sigma of 0.175 for the month (1-yr realized vol 73% [4] implies ~0.21/month; trimmed slightly since vol has eased from the June-July spike, but kept above annual/3.5 of a normal year because of the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of (1) NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$5.17 x 29.5x peer-median forward P/E = $152.5 (50%), (2) Springboard-implied 2028 EPS ~$5.01 x 29.5x = $148 (30%), (3) historical base-rate anchor: median 12m forward return of +6% after GLW's prior +60% years = $166 (20%); blended ~$154.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027 consensus EPS $4.37; 2028 EPS est. $5.46 (+25%); NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$5.17; x 29.5x (peer median fwd P/E, 12 peers)

inputs_detail.derivation: Below the 33.08% 3Y EPS growth forecast [3] and the +33% 2027 consensus growth [2], because Springboard's sales CAGR is 19% (Q4'26-Q4'30) [1] and Q3 guide shows EPS +28% on sales +16% [1]: 19% sales growth plus some operating leverage, less ~1.5% ATM dilution [9], gives ~25%. 4.37 x 1.25 = 5.46.
5.46 / 1.25^0.25 = 5.17 (one quarter of 2027 run-rate, three quarters of 2028).

Peer median fwd P/E 29.49x (12 peers, range 11.8x-50.7x). GLW's 3Y EPS growth forecast 33.1% [3] sits just below the peer median of 36.6%, and GLW's history (2000-02 bust, [5]) argues against a premium, so the median is used. GLW currently trades at 42.3x [3].

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Springboard-implied: 2028 sales ~$27B x 16.5% core net margin / 890M shares = EPS $5.01 x 29.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: Between 2027 consensus revenue $23.10B [2] and the company's $30B annualized run-rate target for end-2028 [1]; a linear ramp from ~$25B (early 2028) to $30B (end-2028) averages ~$27B.
Q2'26 core net income 0.78 x 875M = $682M on $4,738M core sales = 14.4%; Q3 guide midpoint 0.87 x 875M = $761M on $4.95B = 15.4% [1]. Extrapolating ~0.5pt/yr leverage gives 16.5% in 2028.
875M Q2 diluted [1] + up to $2B ATM [9] at ~$150 = ~13M shares -> ~888-890M.
Same peer median as method 1; 5.01 x 29.5 = $147.8.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Base rate: in GLW monthly history since 1999, 43 overlapping month-ends with trailing 12m return > +60% had median forward 12m return +6% (40% negative, range -91% to +122%); 156.68 x 1.06

inputs_detail.input: Median forward 12m return after +60% trailing year
inputs_detail.derivation: Computed from Twelve Data monthly closes 1999-2026 [5]: episodes 2000, 2003-04, 2005-06, 2009-10, 2020-21, 2025; median +6%, mean +4.7%, 39.5% negative. Unconditional median is +9% with 40% negative, so a big run carries little predictive information except fatter tails.

bear.story: AI capex digestion: S&P's 2027 forecast of $1.3T hyperscaler capex [8] with FCF negative for 5 of 6 spenders invites a pause; Optical orders slow, Springboard run-rate slips, and the multiple compresses toward the cyclical-cabling end of the peer range (BDC 11.8x, TEL 17.5x). ~$5.0 NTM EPS x ~19x = $95. History shows this path is real: GLW fell from ~$109 (2000) to $1.60 (2002) when fiber capex reversed [5], and fell ~50% in July 2026 without any fundamental miss [4,24].

base.story: Corning hits roughly its $20B end-2026 and stays on track for $30B end-2028 [1]; 2027 EPS near the $4.37 consensus [2]; multiple de-rates from 42x NTM to the ~29-30x peer median as growth normalizes, so price is roughly flat despite ~25-30% EPS growth.

bull.story: Capex keeps surprising upward (consensus capex has been too low two years running) and optical/fiber shortages persist; Springboard is raised again and 2028 EPS approaches the 33% 3Y CAGR path (~$5.8) [3]; GLW holds a high-30s multiple, retesting the June record ($255 close [4]).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium: GLW's 3Y EPS growth forecast (33.1%) is slightly below the peer median (36.6%), and about half its sales (Glass Innovations, Automotive, Solar, Life Sciences [1]) grow slower than pure AI optics names; its 25-year price history shows deeper cyclical drawdowns than the cabling peers [5]. No discount either: Optical Communications is 44% of Q2 sales ($2,072M of $4,738M) and grew 32% [1], comparable to the AI-networking peers. Hence the median.

thesis_break_reason: $110 is below the July 28 post-earnings capitulation low ($114.50 intraday, $124.05 close [4]) and equals ~21x the $5.17 NTM EPS path; trading there would most likely mean the market is pricing an actual cut to the Springboard trajectory or a hyperscaler capex pause (the bear case), not ordinary volatility in a stock with 73% realized vol.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler capex: S&P sees +50% in 2027 to $1.3T but FCF negative for 5 of 6 spenders and capex flattening in 2028 [8]; a flattening 2028 is exactly when the Oct-2027 price is set.
Multiple: GLW at 42x NTM vs 29.5x peer median; de-rating alone can offset a year of EPS growth.
Regime volatility: 73% realized vol and index/flow-driven moves (June FTSE Russell reclassification spike, July unwind [24]) make the 12-month outcome very wide.
Dilution and capital intensity: the $2B ATM [9] suggests capacity spending is outrunning internal cash.
Non-optical segments (Glass Innovations, Automotive, Solar) carry lower growth and their own cycles [1].
Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available from sourced pages; the EV/EBITDA comparison uses TTM.
reasoning: Lane: base rates. (1) Own history [5]: across 1999-2026 the 12m log-return distribution for GLW has 10th/50th/90th percentiles of -0.59/+0.10/+0.68; after years with >+60% trailing gains (now +80% [4]) the forward median is +6% with ~40% negative, i.e. a hot run predicts little except fat tails, and the 2000-02 fiber bust (-98%) is the precedent for the left tail. (2) The stock is already in a volatile topping pattern: record $255.69 close on 2026-06-29 on index reclassification [4,24], ~50% drawdown into the July print, chop between $124 and $173 since [4]; 1-yr realized vol 73% [4]. (3) Macro/event odds: Kalshi 2027 recession 20% (record low, 2026-09-26) [6]; Polymarket AI-industry downturn by end-2026 6.1% ($2.44M vol) and by mid-2027 18.5% (thin) [7]; I treat ~20-25% odds of a capex-digestion shock within the horizon as the bear weight. (4) Fundamentals (filing [1], consensus [2]) give strong growth (Q3 guide EPS +28%, 2027 EPS $4.37), but at a 29.5x peer-median multiple the Oct-2027 value is ~$148-153, close to spot, so growth is mostly priced in and the forecast is roughly centred on today's price. Ladder = mixture of lognormals: bear 25% (median $95, sigma 0.50), base 50% ($160, 0.25), bull 25% ($225, 0.30); median ~$160, mean ~$168; P(>=157)=0.53. Tails kept fatter than a normal large cap (P(<94)=13%, P(>=274)=7.6%) to match GLW's own 10th/90th percentile history and current vol, with the 1999-2002 drawdown driving the ~1.5% mass below $39. Source mix: the mandatory 12-peer comps (12 data pages, out of lane) push the in-lane share to 9 of 24 sources (~38%), below the 60% target; all in-lane sources are base-rate, price-history, prediction-market or capex-cycle material. Twelve Data statistics/estimates endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus came from StockAnalysis. Several capex pages (Moody's/DCD, ts2.tech) returned 403 and were not used.
